key_insight: ISLA builds physical invariances into a transformer for steady, boundary-driven PDEs, preserving predictions across rigid motions, reflections, unit changes, and mesh refinement.
engineering_relevance: More consistent predictions across poses, units, and boundary meshes could make aerodynamic surrogates more reliable in engineering workflows.
method: Uses distances and relative angles to learned slice anchors, never feeding coordinates directly into learned operations.
Treats boundary cells as tokens, weights boundary sums by quadrature, and normalizes lengths using a boundary-derived scale.
Predicts interior fields through a tree-accelerated learned boundary kernel, with each query independent of other queries.
evidence_signal: On AeroZoo’s 2,816 flows, mean reference-scaled velocity and pressure errors were at least 3.1× and 3.3× lower than any baseline’s; on AirfRANS, ISLA ranked second to GLOBE.
watch_item: The abstract addresses steady, boundary-driven PDEs; performance on unsteady flows and broader PDE classes remains unestablished.
paper_title: ISLA: A Coordinate-Free, Measure-Weighted Transformer for Boundary-Driven PDEs
